newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oil union threatens strike after arrests.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil union threatens strike after arrests.

text.p: Colombia's main oil workers' union threatened an all-out strike after 13 of its members were arrested Thursday on suspicion of carrying out dynamite attacks on the country's oil pipelines, union heads said.
A final decision on the strike will be taken at an extraordinary meeting Monday but USO leader Hernando Hernandez indicated it was a foregone conclusion.
"We've taken a decision to call a strike. I don't believe our response (to the arrests) can be any other than to stage a strike," Hernandez said.
A USO supervisor and 11 oil workers were arrested by agents of the chief prosecutor's office at their homes and at work in northeast Norte de Santander province Thursday morning.
USO treasurer and former chairman, Cesar Carrillo, was seized as he left the headquarters of state oil company Ecopetrol in the afternoon.

A spokesman at the prosecutor's office declined to say on what grounds the oilmen had been arrested. But USO social services secretary Gustavo Triana said the men were being accused of terrorist acts.

The country's main oil pipeline, from Cano Limon in the northeast to Covenas on the Caribbean coast, is a favorite target of National Liberation Army (ELN). It has been blown up more than 40 times this year, causing more than $38 million in lost production and damage.

The authorities have accused the 5,700-strong USO union, known for its fiercely nationalistic stance, of backing the ELN, which specializes in attacks on foreign multinationals and oil infrastructure. Triana denied there was any formal link between the union and the outlawed rebel army, Colombia's second largest.

A 24-hour strike by the USO in mid-October paralyzed pumping operations for the first time in its history along the country's two main pipelines. Triana said USO was likely to decide Monday on an indefinite strike to protest at the most recent arrests but also at plans to divide up Ecopetrol activities.
Two USO workers were arrested in Cucuta, in Norte de Santander in August. They are currently in custody accused of rebellion.
